'''Virgil Percec''' (born December 8, 1946)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://web.sas.upenn.edu/percecgroup/professor-percec/|title=Professor Virgil Percec – Percec Research Laboratory|website=web.sas.upenn.edu}}</ref> is a [[Romanian-American]] chemist and [[P. Roy Vagelos]] Chair and Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. Expert in [[Organic chemistry|organic]], [[Macromolecular chemistry|macromolecular]] and [[Supramolecular chemistry|supramolecular]] chemistry including [[self-assembly]], biological membrane [[Mimicry|mimics]], complex [[chiral]] [[complex systems|systems]], and  [[catalysis]].  Pioneered the fields of [[liquid crystals]] with complex architecture,<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.sas.upenn.edu/sasalum/newsltr/fall05/SASMagFa05_webfinb.pdf#page=11 | title=The Molecular Architect |page=11}}</ref> supramolecular [[dendrimers]], [[Janus particles|Janus]] dendrimers and glycodendrimers, organic [[Frank-Kasper phases]] and [[quasicrystals]], supramolecular [[polymers]], helical [[chirality]], [[Nickel(II) precatalysts|Ni-catalyzed]] [[Cross-coupling reaction|cross-coupling]] and multiple [[Living polymerization|living]] and self-interrupted [[polymerization]]s. Most of these concepts were inspired by [[Nature]] and [[biology|biological principles]].

== Life ==
=== Early life===
Percec was born in December 1946 in [[Siret]], Romania. His father, Traian, was a schoolteacher and painter; his mother was named Virginia. Virgil attended [[Eudoxiu Hurmuzachi National College|Eudoxiu Hurmuzachi High School]] in [[Rădăuți]].<ref name="acad">{{cite web|url=https://acad.ro/institutia/media_virgil_percec.html|title="Profesorul Cristofor Simionescu a fost unul dintre marii oameni de știință români" – dialog cu prof. Virgil Percec despre mentorul său|language=ro|first=Cătălin|last= Mosoia|publisher=[[Romanian Academy]]|website=acad.ro|date=July 31, 2018|access-date=August 14, 2024}}</ref>

=== Education ===
Percec received his BS in [[Organic chemistry|Organic]] and [[Macromolecular Chemistry]] at the [[Gheorghe Asachi Technical University of Iași|Polytechnic University in Iași]] in 1969 and his PhD in 1976 at the Institute of Macromolecular Chemistry in Iași<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://icmpp.ro/|title=Home - Institute of Macromolecular Chemistry "Petru Poni" Iași|website=icmpp.ro}}</ref> where he had {{ill|Cristofor Simionescu|ro|Cristofor I. Simionescu}} as a mentor. In 1981 he defected from his native country and after short postdoctoral stays at the [[University of Freiburg]] in [[Germany]] (July 1981 with H.-J. Cantow) and [[University of Akron]], US (August 1981 to March 1982 with J. P. Kennedy) he joined the Department of Macromolecular Science of [[Case Western Reserve University]] (CWRU) in [[Cleveland]], US in March 1982 as an assistant professor. He was promoted to associate professor in 1984 and to professor in 1986. In 1991 he became director of [[Materials Research Science and Engineering Centers]] (MRSEC) and in 1993, he was awarded the Leonard Case Jr. Chair at CWRU. In 1999 he moved to the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in [[Philadelphia]] as P. Roy Vagelos Chair and Professor of Chemistry. He has been repeatedly a visiting professor at the Universities of [[University of Freiburg|Freiburg]], [[Ulm University|Ulm]] and at the [[Max Planck Institute]] for Polymer Research in [[Mainz]] (all in Germany) and at the [[Royal Institute of Technology]] in [[Stockholm, Sweden]].

=== Personal life===
Percec and his wife, Simona, have a daughter Ivona Percec.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pennmedicine.org/cosmetic-services/meet-the-team/meet-the-doctors/ivona-percec|title=Ivona Percec, MD, PhD - Penn Medicine Cosmetic Services|website=www.pennmedicine.org}}</ref> She earned a double major in Molecular Biology and Medieval History from [[Princeton University]] and received an MD and PhD in Genetics from [[University of Pennsylvania]], where she joined the faculty and surgery department.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.med.upenn.edu/apps/faculty/index.php/g275/p14458|title=Ivona Percec &#124; Faculty &#124; About Us &#124; Perelman School of Medicine &#124; Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania}}</ref>

== Research ==

== Awards and achievements ==
Percec is the author of more than 800 scientific articles, 20 books and special issues and listed as inventor of at least 80 patents. Percec presented over 1200 endowed, plenary and invited lectures. He has served as the  Editor of Journal of Polymer Science: Part A: Polymer Chemistry, Advances in Polymer Science and Book Series “Liquid Crystals”. He serves on Editorial and Advisory Scientific Boards of 24 International Journals, and of the advisory boards of many Academic and Industrial Institutions. Percec organized numerous National and International Symposia including Gordon Conferences, and IUPAC meetings. In 2018, Percec was listed as "Global Highly Cited Researches" by Clarivate Analytics for world-class researches and their exceptional research performance based on multiple highly cited papers that rank in the top 1% by citations for field and year in Web of Sciences. In 2016, 2015, and 2014 he was listed as "One of The World's Most Influential Scientific Minds of our Time" by Thomson Reuters. Percec delivered over 1400 plenary endowed lectures including: the Raychem Lecturer, Chemistry Department, University of California, Berkeley, CA (1996); The 4th Aggarwal Lecturer in Polymer Science, Chemistry Department, Cornell University, NY (1997); The Inaugural Woodward Lecturer "Frontiers in Chemical Sciences", Harvard University (2004); the 7th Rohm and Haas Lecture at the University of California, Berkeley (2005); the Lecturer of the Swiss Chemical Society (2008); Invited Lecture at Kekule Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry at the [[University of Bonn]] (2010);<ref>Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211208/WX0Oaf-2dfk Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20210607153240/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WX0Oaf-2dfk Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite AV media| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WX0Oaf-2dfk| title = Bioinspired synthesis of complex functional systems | website=[[YouTube]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref> the Inaugural Kavli Foundation Innovations in Chemistry Lecture and Award,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cen.acs.org/sponsored-content/acs-kavli-lectures.html | title=ACS Kavli lectures highlight the biggest, the smallest, and the most complex| access-date=2023-12-24}}</ref> American Chemical Society (2011); The 8th International Dendrimer Symposium (2013);<ref>{{cite web| url=https://blogs.rsc.org/nj/2013/09/04/highlights-of-the-8th-international-dendrimer-symposium/?doing_wp_cron=1623076291.7154760360717773437500 | title=Highlights of the 8th International Dendrimer Symposium | access-date=2023-12-24}}</ref> the Inaugural Aldrich lecture at Massachusetts Institute of Technology (2015); Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Israel, Department of Chemistry and the Faculty of Natural Science's Distinguished Scientist Visitor and Lecturers (2016); IVA 100: Centennial Jubilee Workshop of the Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences (2019).<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y-2dXUhCqAI&t=16010s | title=Jubileumsseminarium: Materialens betydelse i samhället | website=youtube.com| language=sv}}</ref> Percec is an Honorary Foreign Member of the Romanian Academy (1993), Doctor Honoris Causa of University of Athens (Greece), Polytechnic University Iasi (Romania) since 2007 and of Polytechnic University, Bucharest (2016). He is an Honorary Member of the Israel Chemical Society (2009) and of the Romanian Society of Chemistry and "Petru Poni" Medal of the Romanian Society of Chemistry (2014). Percec educated over 300 PhD and postdoctoral students with more than 70 of them being in faculty positions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://web.sas.upenn.edu/percecgroup/group-members/|title=Group Members – Percec Research Laboratory|access-date=2021-05-24|archive-date=2021-05-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210524163301/https://web.sas.upenn.edu/percecgroup/group-members/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

*2002, [https://www.ptn.nu/ptn-medema-lecture-award/ Polymer Technology Netherland (PTN) Award] from the Netherlands.
